title: POC TTFT hybrid routing triage
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on TTFT (time-to-first-token) and hybrid routing options. Agreed next steps: Connor to run microbench with hybrid routing enabled, Dana/Liam to provide production seqlen histograms, Maya to send updated pricing for a 3-week reserved pilot and security checklist.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 10:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Hsu (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (CTO - CartoMetrics), Liam O'Connell (ML Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Eng Manager)

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda—status on the TTFT regressions we saw last week, hybrid routing experiment, and stream handshakes, then we'll decide bench steps.
[00:00:12] Dana: Yep, thanks. we had a couple of customer incidents where first token is spiky during burst hours, so that's why we want deep into TTFT.
[00:00:20] Connor: quick note, we instrumented the pilot nodes with 1ms granularity histograms, the microburst traces show a bimodal distribution, looks like KV cache warmup is a big factor.
[00:00:30] Liam: when you say KV warmup, are we talking cold-starts across all shards or a localized miss pattern? we saw high cross-shard misses when sequence length > 800.
[00:00:42] Connor: mostly localized. the cache policy we ran on the test pool has a small prefix cache size; when our prefix seqlen distribution spikes the model evicts entries and that adds like 5-12 ms to the first token path.
[00:00:55] Priya: And is that consistent across quantization modes? we tried int8 on the last run.
[00:01:02] Connor: int8 does shave some compute time, but the cache miss penalty is independent — it's IO + deserialization + re-populating KV. so int8 helps token emission but not the warmup.
[00:01:12] Maya: ok—two threads then: reduce cache misses and evaluate hybrid routing to see if routing to a reserved pool for likely-hot prefixes helps.
[00:01:22] Dana: Can you define hybrid routing again? last time you used the term but our infra team wanted a plain language summary.
[00:01:30] Connor: Sure—hybrid routing is a policy in Redwood's routing layer that decides per-request whether to route to Dedicated hot pool (lower latency, higher $) or to the shared Hosted pool (lower cost, higher variability) based on heuristics: prefix match score, client SLAs, and seqlen. it can do lightweight scoring in the front proxy and fall back if capacity isn't available.
[00:01:52] Liam: So we'd be paying premium for a subset of requests? what's the granularity—per-call or per-client?
[00:01:58] Maya: per-call. we only route calls that match your hot-prefix set or have a SLA flag. you'll still have many calls on Hosted. It gives you predictable TTFT for prioritized requests.
[00:02:10] Dana: That might work, our priority flows are 12% of traffic but account for 60% of primetime load.
[00:02:17] Priya: question—what's the handshake cost for streaming with hybrid routing? we stream responses and don't want to double-handshake.
[00:02:24] Connor: good question. currently streaming handshake includes a small upfront tokenization + proto handshake. if we route mid-stream it's a full redirect. however, with the 'sticky connection' option we can pin the connection for short windows and avoid re-handshake in many cases—there's a slight increase in connection resource usage but TTFT improves for subsequent messages.
[00:02:45] Dana: sticky sounds promising, but do we have metrics on connection churn?
[00:02:50] Connor: we pulled sandbox traces—connection churn is about 8% per minute under load peaks; enabling sticky reduces visible TTFT variance by about 18% in our toy workloads. i'll share the CSV.
[00:03:02] Maya: Great. Let's look at the kernel selection questions. last week you saw pathological kernel choices when seqlen varied, correct?
[00:03:09] Liam: yes—our distribution has a long tail; most requests are 128-256 tokens but we have 3% at 2k. the runtime sometimes picks a kernel optimized for long seqlen that is suboptimal for the bulk.
[00:03:22] Connor: Right—the runtime's kernel selector is heuristics-based: it looks at the requested max seqlen, batch composition, and hardware topology. if a batch mixes 2k and 128 it tends to pick the long-seq kernel which increases latency for the 128 ones. We can enable batching-aware hedging: split batches by seqlen cluster and run parallel kernels, then return earliest outputs. there's a small extra compute cost but big TTFT wins.
[00:03:46] Priya: Is that supported in Dedicated? we can't afford large compute overhead if traffic grows.
[00:03:53] Connor: yes it's supported as an opt-in runtime mode—'hedged seqlen batching'. compute overhead depends on duplication factor; in our internal tests a duplication factor of 1.2 yields 30% reduction in median TTFT for mixed batches with only ~10% extra tokens processed.
[00:04:08] Dana: can we see a side-by-side of hedged batching vs hybrid routing for our priority flows?
[00:04:14] Maya: that's actionable. Connor, can you run a microbench comparing three configs: baseline, hedged batching, hybrid routing (sticky enabled) with our sample seqlen histogram?
[00:04:24] Connor: yes. i'll run 1h runs with synthetic inter-arrival times to mirror your peak burst and produce CSVs with p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and total token cost.
[00:04:34] Liam: Also include KV hit/miss rates and avg cache fill time.
[00:04:38] Connor: noted.
[00:04:40] Priya: question on fallbacks—if Dedicated pool is saturated, does hybrid routing automatically fall back to hosted and do we get a degraded SLA?
[00:04:48] Maya: yes automatic fallback is built-in. you can configure fallback policy: immediate fallback, queue-wait, or degrade to lower model. each has tradeoffs—immediate fallback reduces failed requests but increases latency variance.
[00:04:59] Dana: for us, predictable TTFT matters more than occasional higher cost. we prefer queue-wait for a short window and then fallback. can that be configured per-prefix?
[00:05:08] Maya: yes per-prefix or per-SLA tag. we'll include that in the config doc.
[00:05:12] Liam: security question—if we route some calls to hosted pools, how do we ensure data residency and KMS usage?
[00:05:20] Connor: in hybrid mode you can mark prefixes as "private"—those never leave your VPC/Dedicated. For others, hosted receives encrypted payloads and we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for at-rest encryption. i'll attach the security checklist.
[00:05:33] Dana: Good. we need SOC2 + audit log details in that checklist.
[00:05:37] Maya: I'll include SOC2 section; we already have SOC2 Type II reports and will add logging fields you can audit.
[00:05:44] Liam: back to kernels—what about quantization interplay? last run with int8 had slightly higher variance in p99.
[00:05:52] Connor: that's expected; quantization affects throughput but sometimes increases tail latency due to compute kernel differences. For p99-sensitive workloads we recommend mixed precision or per-route quantization profiles—use int8 for non-priority flows and fp16 or bf16 for priority.
[00:06:06] Priya: can we do per-route quant profiles in the POC?
[00:06:09] Connor: yes, we can configure per-route profile, and we'll include model variant fallback in the experiment.
[00:06:15] Maya: cool. i want to capture exact deliverables for this week. Connor—microbench matrix, include hedged batching and hybrid routing sticky option, CSVs with p50/p95/p99 and KV miss rates. include cost estimate delta. Dana/Liam—supply seqlen histograms and sample prompt set. Maya—send pilot pricing and security checklist. any other items?
[00:06:36] Dana: one more—can you add a smoke test we can run in our sandbox with a single script to validate TTL of KV? we want something ops can run quickly.
[00:06:44] Connor: yes, we'll provide a small smoke harness script in Python and curl examples.
[00:06:49] Priya: timeline for next sync?
[00:06:52] Maya: reconvene next Tuesday 2026-03-10 10:00Z. I'll book the invite.
[00:07:00] Liam: quick FYI—we may have procurement questions about reserved pool commitment length. what's the minimum?
[00:07:06] Maya: standard pilot reserved is 3 weeks minimum for a pilot; production commitments start at 3 months. I'll include pricing tiers in the doc.
[00:07:14] Dana: ok that helps.
[00:07:17] Connor: i'll flag one more risk—if your traffic pattern gets more spiky than projected the hedged batching duplication cost could exceed estimates. we'll include sensitivity tests in the microbench.
[00:07:29] Maya: good call. anything else?
[00:07:32] (silence)
[00:07:36] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the notes and action items.

Recap:
- Connor to run microbench (baseline / hedged batching / hybrid routing sticky) and share CSV + cost delta (due 2026-03-06).
- Dana to upload production seqlen histograms and sample prompts (due 2026-03-05).
